title: NeoMundi Evidence — pilot submission manifest
description: What a third party hands us. EVERYTHING in this document is a DECLARATION by the submitter. Ingestion recomputes the digests and the sizes of the declared artefacts, and verifies any attestation against the published trust store; it verifies NOTHING else, and never promotes a declaration to an attested fact. The split is reported line by line: CONTROLLED (we recomputed it), DECLARED (their word, kept verbatim), NOT DEMONSTRABLE (no control could establish it from this submission).

submission_id.description: Stable identifier chosen by the submitter. Never reused for a different submission.

submitted_at_declared.description: DECLARED by the submitter. No trusted clock takes part, and ingestion never reads its own clock to contradict it.

pilot.description: DECLARED identity of the submitter. Ingestion does not verify it, and cannot: nothing in a file establishes who wrote it.

reference_declared.description: A ticket, contract or engagement reference, if any. Declared.

execution.description: What the submitter says was executed. All DECLARED. A digest here is only a claim until the artefact carrying the bytes is supplied and recomputed.

parameters_declared.description: Kept VERBATIM. Never normalised: a normalised parameter set is no longer the one that was sent.

artifacts.description: The files that carry the bytes. Each one is RECOMPUTED at ingestion: this is the only part of the submission that ingestion can establish.

path.description: RELATIVE path inside the submission, with forward slashes. Absolute paths, drive letters, `..` segments and symbolic links are REFUSED -- a submission must not be able to name a file outside itself.

role.description: What the submitter says this file is. Declared: ingestion does not parse the file to confirm its role.

attestations.description: Detached signatures the submitter already holds. Verified by `verify_attestation.py` -- the SAME verifier an auditor uses, invoked unchanged, its verdict reported verbatim. No second signature engine exists.

trust_store_declared.description: Which store the submitter believes vouches for it. Ingestion uses the store the OPERATOR supplies, never one carried by the submission: a package must not carry its own answer to whether its signer is trustworthy.

provenance_declared.description: Declared provenance of the execution environment. Absent fields are reported ABSENT, never defaulted and never null-filled -- the same discipline as an unmeasured signal.

limits_declared.description: What the submitter states their own package does NOT establish. Kept verbatim and reported: a submitter who names their limits is easier to trust than one who names none.

instant.description: UTC, second precision, trailing Z. DECLARED in every case.
